extracted.intended_audience: Researchers at German research institutions preparing applications to establish or renew a DFG Research Unit
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for establishing, structuring, and renewing a Research Unit funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG), including eligibility, required scientific quality, networking expectations, funding modules and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Funding — close-knit, medium-term cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Close-knit, medium-term cooperation between several researchers with an outstanding track record who work on a defined research task with the aim of achieving results that go well beyond what would be possible with individual grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding aims to provide personnel and material resources for medium-term close cooperation (usually designed to last eight years). Research Units often contribute to establishing new research directions and can be integrated into overarching research-policy initiatives (e.g., Clinical Research Units, Centres for Advanced Studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures to promote early career researchers and equity/diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures tailored specifically to the Research Unit are pursued in order to promote researchers in early career phases and also equity and diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programme allows funding of network measures and includes a 'Standard Allowance for Equity and Diversity' module. Research Units can offer development opportunities, temporary relief from teaching/administrative duties, and strengthen non-university cooperation and international collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical composition and institutional base
rubrics_metrics.description: A Research Unit typically comprises fewer than ten projects which are coordinated so as to enable work on a common research topic. The majority of the research projects are to be based at universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure may vary by research question, disciplines involved and intended structural impact; applicants should design coordination to enable common-topic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — applicant institutions and researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers in all disciplines at German research institutions who have completed their academic training (as a rule, those holding a doctorate) are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not eligible: members of organisations that serve purely commercial purposes; members of organisations who are not permitted to publish their results in a publicly accessible form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific quality and originality of the research endeavour must be internationally competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same quality criteria apply as for research grants; Research Units should demonstrate international competitiveness in significance and originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close, medium-term collaboration within a network
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Unit must demonstrate close, medium-term collaboration within a network of researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration should be structured to achieve synergy and outcomes beyond individual projects, with coordinated project planning and shared research goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear added value of network funding vs individual grants
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a clear added value of funding as a network compared to individual grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should justify why a Research Unit (network funding) enables research outcomes or structural effects that individual grants could not achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincing working hypotheses and well-defined research topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must present convincing working hypotheses and a well-defined research topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research plans should articulate testable hypotheses and a coherent thematic focus that binds the projects together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of project leaders and spokesperson suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Project leaders must have appropriate qualifications, and the designated spokesperson must be suitable to lead the Research Unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors will consider track record, leadership ability, and suitability of the spokesperson to coordinate the unit; include CVs and evidence of prior accomplishment/leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type and scope of funding — available modules
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme offers various funding modules to cover personnel, workshops, coordination, network measures and other needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available modules include: Basic Module; Temporary Positions for Principal Investigators; Replacements; Temporary Substitutes for Clinicians; Professorships; Mercator Fellows; Project-Specific Workshops; Start-Up Funding; Coordination; Network Funds; Public Relations; Standard Allowance for Equity and Diversity. Emmy Noether Groups and Heisenberg programme funding recipients can be associated with a Research Unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is generally up to eight years, divided into two funding periods of four years each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and planning should reflect this typical timeframe and specify milestones/outputs across the periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission rules and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft proposals and establishment proposals can be submitted at any time; revised draft proposals may be re-submitted only once. Renewal proposals must be submitted six months before the end of the current funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to consult the responsible DFG department at an early stage regarding intended submission dates. Follow the Forms and Guidelines provided by the DFG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft-proposal review process
rubrics_metrics.description: A draft proposal submitted by the designated spokesperson is first reviewed by at least two external experts and then assessed by the relevant review board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on the review board, draft proposals are considered either on a regular basis or at selected meetings. Based on the review board’s recommendation, the DFG Senate decides whether to recommend elaboration of an establishment proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment/renewal decision process and bodies involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment or renewal proposals are discussed by a panel that includes external reviewers, members of the relevant review boards and a member of the DFG Senate; the DFG Joint Committee makes final funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel provides a recommendation; based on reviews and a Senate recommendation, the Joint Committee decides whether to fund or continue funding. The Joint Committee meets to decide on Research Units four times a year.

rubrics_metrics.name: International collaboration support
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG provides funding and mechanisms to support international collaboration by Research Units and foreign cooperation partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support includes travel funds and guest funds for foreign partners under the Basic Module; travel funds and remuneration for foreign partners under the Mercator Fellows module; travel funds under Project-Specific Workshops; funds for project implementation by foreign partners via transfer under special procedures (e.g., Cooperation with the Middle East, Developing Countries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional direct submission by foreign researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: By way of an exception, proposals can be submitted directly by a foreign researcher to the DFG if the project abroad makes an important additional contribution and adds significant value to the Research Unit's goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such direct submissions are allowed only where the foreign researcher’s project substantially enhances the unit’s objectives; consult DFG Head Office on feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support via partner organisations and lead-agency procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperation may be supported by foreign partner organisations through D-A-CH, D-Lux, and D-Süd lead-agency procedures or joint proposal submission agreements with Austria/Switzerland, Luxembourg, and South Tyrol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint proposal routes or individual agreements with academic institutions abroad are possible but require prior consultation with the DFG Head Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early contact with DFG programme contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are advised to consult the department responsible at the DFG Head Office at an early stage regarding their intended submission date for draft, establishment, or renewal proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early consultation supports better planning and helps align submission timing, eligibility questions, and international cooperation arrangements with DFG procedures.
